proposals.before: When Dou Yun governed Jingzhao he put hundreds to death, and the hoodlums gradually learned to fear and quiet down.
proposals.after: When Dou Yu governed Jingzhao he put hundreds to death, and the hoodlums gradually learned to fear and quiet down.
proposals.reason: Chinese 竇潏 is Dou Yu; Yun is a wrong English rendering of 潏.

proposals.before: Dou Yun governed Jingzhao and killed as many as several hundred people; gradually they became fearful and restrained themselves.
proposals.after: Dou Yu governed Jingzhao and killed as many as several hundred people; gradually they became fearful and restrained themselves.
proposals.reason: Chinese 竇潏 should be Dou Yu, not Dou Yun.

proposals.before: Hunqing feigned defeat and tried to slip away, but his men seized him. Renhou said, “This fool is not worth addressing.”
proposals.after: Hunqing’s ruse ran out and he tried to slip away, but officers seized him. Renhou said, “This fool is not worth addressing.”
proposals.reason: 詐窮 means his deception was exhausted, not that he feigned defeat; 吏執之 are officers, not his men.

proposals.before: Han Qiuzhi, the great bandit already captured, proclaimed to the stockades, “Whoever dares come out will be beheaded!”
proposals.after: Han Qiu, knowing the great bandit had already been captured, proclaimed to the stockades, “Whoever dares come out will be beheaded!”
proposals.reason: 韓求知 is Han Qiu plus the verb 知, not a fused name Han Qiuzhi.

proposals.before: Yang Shili, military governor of Eastern Chuan, had begun in the Shence Army and rose to Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Councillor.
proposals.after: Yang Shili, military governor of Eastern Chuan, had begun in the Shence Army and rose to Acting Minister of Works and Joint Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
proposals.reason: 檢校司空 is Acting Sikong (Minister of Works), not Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

proposals.before: Eastern Chuan military governor Yang Shili at first belonged to the Shence Army and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and equal associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
proposals.after: Eastern Chuan military governor Yang Shili at first belonged to the Shence Army and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Minister of Works and equal associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
proposals.reason: 司空 is Minister of Works; Grand Master of Splendid Happiness is a mistranslation.

proposals.before: Thereupon Shi’an dared not come out; Shili personally supervised the troops; in ten battles all were defeated northward.
proposals.after: Thereupon Shi’an dared not come out; Shili personally supervised the troops; in ten battles all were defeated.
proposals.reason: 皆北 uses 北 meaning routed or defeated, not geographic northward.

proposals.before: Zhao Chou, a man of Wanqiu in Chen prefecture, for generations served as yamen generals of the Zhongwu Army.
proposals.after: Zhao Chou, a man of Wanqiu in Chen prefecture; for generations his family served as yamen generals of the Zhongwu Army.
proposals.reason: Literal English attributes multi-generation service to Chou himself; Chinese 世為 marks hereditary family service.

proposals.before: Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and promoted him step by step to Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
proposals.after: Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and promoted him step by step to Acting Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: 檢校司空 is Acting Minister of Works, not Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

proposals.before: Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and repeatedly promoted him to Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
proposals.after: Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and repeatedly promoted him to Acting Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 檢校司空 in the literal English.

proposals.before: Huang Chao, hearing of Kai’s capture, was shocked and furious. He massed his entire army on the Yin River, joined Qin Zongquan for a force of hundreds of thousands, dug five rings of trenches around the city, and assaulted it from every side.
proposals.after: Huang Chao, hearing that Kai was dead, was shocked and furious. He massed his entire army on the Yin River, joined Qin Zongquan for a force of hundreds of thousands, dug five rings of trenches around the city, and assaulted it from every side.
proposals.reason: Chinese 巢聞楷死 says Chao heard Kai was dead; idiomatic wrongly says capture.

proposals.before: He and his younger brother Chang were deeply devoted to one another. In his later years, as age overtook him, he handed all military affairs to Chang, then died and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: He and his younger brother Chang were deeply devoted to one another. In his later years, as age overtook him, he handed all military affairs to Chang, then died and was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: With his younger brother Chang he was extremely affectionate; later, as he grew old, he entrusted all military affairs to him; then he died and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: With his younger brother Chang he was extremely affectionate; later, as he grew old, he entrusted all military affairs to him; then he died and was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: Same 太尉 mistranslation as Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: He died in the second year of Qianning at the age of fifty-three and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: He died in the second year of Qianning at the age of fifty-three and was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: In the second year of Qianning he died, age fifty-three, and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: In the second year of Qianning he died, age fifty-three, and was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
proposals.reason: Same 太尉 mistranslation as Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: At the start of the Tianfu era Han Jian took over the Zhongwu Army and appointed Pin acting governor of Tongzhou circuit.
proposals.after: At the start of the Tianfu era Han Jian took over the Zhongwu Army and appointed Xu acting governor of Tongzhou circuit.
proposals.reason: 珝 is Xǔ; the English personal name Pin does not match the Chinese characters or standard romanization.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Tianfu, Han Jian commanded the Zhongwu Army and had Pin act as Tongzhou circuit military governor designate.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Tianfu, Han Jian commanded the Zhongwu Army and had Xu act as Tongzhou circuit military governor designate.
proposals.reason: 珝 is Xǔ; literal English wrongly renders the personal name as Pin.

proposals.before: When Emperor Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, Pin was summoned to court and given the title “Meritorious Minister Who Welcomed the Imperial Carriage.”
proposals.after: When Emperor Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, Xu was summoned to court and given the title “Meritorious Minister Who Welcomed the Imperial Carriage.”
proposals.reason: Continues the misrendering of 珝 as Pin; should be Xu.

proposals.before: Yet he nursed resentment against Xingmi and Liu and wrote: “Princes hold their domains in service to the Son of Heaven. All streams must flow to the sea—however wildly they rush, they dry up in the end. Better to follow the current forever.
proposals.after: Yet he nursed resentment against Xingmi and Liu and wrote: “Princes hold their domains in service to the Son of Heaven. It is like the hundred streams not paying court to the sea—however wildly they rush and spread, they end as dry earth; better to follow the current without end.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic reverses the Chinese simile 譬百川不朝於海 (streams that do NOT pay court to the sea) into ‘must flow to the sea,’ obscuring Yun’s warning.

proposals.before: Yun sent Li Gao with a letter offering, “Your family is in my hands. Join me and I will divide the realm and make you a king.”
proposals.after: Yun sent Li Gao with a deceitful letter offering, “Your family is in my hands. Join me and I will divide the realm and make you a king.”
proposals.reason: Chinese 詒書 marks the letter as deceitful; the idiomatic English drops that sense present in the literal.

proposals.before: Before long Yun died; his head was sent to Huainan; Xingmi wept; he buried him with commoner rites, also buried Kang Ru, and returned Yuan Guan to Hang.
proposals.after: Before long Yun died; his head was sent to Huainan; Xingmi wept; he buried him with commoner rites, also buried Kang Ru, and returned Yuan Guan to Hangzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 杭 refers to Hangzhou; bare “Hang” is an incomplete place name.

proposals.before: Yun gave him land and a house, welcomed his mother, and treated him like a kinsman—so Wengui served him with all his strength.
proposals.after: Yun gave him land and a house, welcomed his mother, and treated him as a sister’s son—so Wengui served him with all his strength.
proposals.reason: Chinese 以甥事之 specifically means treating him as a sister’s son, not a generic kinsman.

proposals.before: Thereupon he set down bow and arrows and submitted to binding; father and son were beheaded in Yangzhou city.
proposals.after: Thereupon he set down bow and arrows and submitted to binding; father and son were beheaded in the Yangzhou marketplace.
proposals.reason: Chinese 揚州市 means the Yangzhou marketplace, not the city in general.

proposals.before: Zhu Yanzhou came from Shucheng in Luzhou.
proposals.after: Zhu Yanshou came from Shucheng in Luzhou.
proposals.reason: 延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou; the English personal name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Zhu Yanzhou was a man of Shucheng in Luzhou.
proposals.after: Zhu Yanshou was a man of Shucheng in Luzhou.
proposals.reason: 延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou; the English personal name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Xingmi wanted to win loyalty through mercy, but Yanzhou was ruthless in killing.
proposals.after: Xingmi wanted to win loyalty through mercy, but Yanshou was ruthless in killing.
proposals.reason: 延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou; the English personal name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Xingmi wished to bind people’s hearts through leniency, but Yanzhou dared to kill.
proposals.after: Xingmi wished to bind people’s hearts through leniency, but Yanshou dared to kill.
proposals.reason: 延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou; the English personal name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Yangzhou had many thieves in those days. When one was caught, Xingmi would return the stolen goods and release him with the warning, “Do not let Yanzhou know.”
proposals.after: Yangzhou had many thieves in those days. When one was caught, Xingmi would return the stolen goods and release him with the warning, “Do not let Yanshou know.”
proposals.reason: 延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou; the English personal name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: At the time Yangzhou had many bandits; when any were caught, Xingmi would give them what they had stolen and send them away, warning, “Do not let Yanzhou know.”
proposals.after: At the time Yangzhou had many bandits; when any were caught, Xingmi would give them what they had stolen and send them away, warning, “Do not let Yanshou know.”
proposals.reason: 延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou; the English personal name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Then he secretly allowed Yanzhou to execute them.
proposals.after: Then he secretly allowed Yanshou to execute them.
proposals.reason: 延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou; the English personal name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Before long he secretly permitted Yanzhou to kill them.
proposals.after: Before long he secretly permitted Yanshou to kill them.
proposals.reason: 延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou; the English personal name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Earlier, Gao Yanwen of Shouzhou had surrendered his prefecture to Zhu Quanzhong. When Xingmi attacked, the other generals feared the strong walls could not be taken. Yanzhou rallied the men, took the city, and was at once made deputy military governor of Huainan.
proposals.after: Earlier, Gao Yanwen of Shouzhou had surrendered his prefecture to Zhu Quanzhong. When Xingmi attacked, the other generals feared the strong walls could not be taken. Yanshou rallied the men, took the city, and was at once made deputy military governor of Huainan.
proposals.reason: 延壽 is Yanshou, not Yanzhou; the English personal name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Earlier, Shouzhou prefect Gao Yanwen had surrendered the entire prefecture to Zhu Quanzhong; Xingmi raided it; the generals feared the city’s stout walls could not be taken; Yanzhou roused them, captured the city, and was immediately memorialized as Huainan military governor deputy.

proposals.before: Zhu Quanzhong still held Shouchun. Yanzhou led out fresh troops in tight five-man squads under each banner and sent Li Hou with ten banners against the western flank. When Hou was beaten, Yanzhou was about to execute him—but Hou begged for five more banners, fought desperately, and drove Zhu Quanzhong away.
proposals.after: Zhu Quanzhong still held Shouchun. Yanshou led out fresh troops in tight five-man squads under each banner and sent Li Hou with ten banners against the western flank. When Hou was beaten, Yanshou was about to execute him—but Hou begged for five more banners, fought desperately, and drove Zhu Quanzhong away.

proposals.after: While Emperor Zhaozong was at Fengxiang, Yanshou was ordered to besiege Cai and relieve Zhu Quanzhong’s pressure, and was promoted to military governor of the Fengguo Army.

proposals.before: Whenever Zhu Quanzhong’s troops came up, Yanzhou would open his gates without preparing defenses—yet they never dared press him.
proposals.after: Whenever Zhu Quanzhong’s troops came up, Yanshou would open his gates without preparing defenses—yet they never dared press him.
